text:
anya: Heads-up — Opal Health finetune onboarding. We merged their LoRA adapters into the 13B base and ran an int4 quant pass on the R4 infra. Quick eval pack shows a big quality drop on multi-turn intents. attaching summary.
kevin: ugh. do you have the pre-quant numbers vs post-quant? rough metrics?
anya: pre-quant intent acc ~92% on our internal S-100 set, post-merge+int4 dropped to ~74%. ROUGE-L down 6 pts, hallucination examples jumped. Perplexity ~1.8x higher on long-context (>1024 tokens).
liam: sounds like adapter chaining/order or kv cache issue. did you try swapping merge order (adapter A then B vs B then A)?
anya: yes — swap improved some examples. order A->B kept the drop; B->A recovers ~10-12% of the loss but still not back to baseline. suggests non-commutative merge behavior.
nora: any tokenizer changes? Opal uses a slightly different tokenizer trimming settings earlier — could be token id shift causing kv misalignment.
anya: checked token ids: base tokenizer identical, but their finetune script used byte fallback for emoji which changed sequence length in a few test cases. I don't think that's the main issue though.
liam: share a minimal repro that runs the two merge variants + int4 export? can test local quant kernels.
anya: posted command run in infra (R4-staging):
```
python3 eval_pack.py --model base-13b --merge loraA,loraB --quant int4 --batch 8 --ctx 2048 --evalset s-100
python3 eval_pack.py --model base-13b --merge loraB,loraA --quant int4 --batch 8 --ctx 2048 --evalset s-100
```
liam: nice. what about running float16 (no quant) after merge to confirm it's quant-specific? if float16 is fine then quant kernels or KV layout likely.
anya: float16 merged runs are near baseline (90-93%). so yep, quant path triggers regression.
kevin: could be per-layer folding differences during merge. Did the merge tool apply bias correction / rescale? our int4 export expects merged weights in a specific order.
anya: merge used standard stitch tool v0.9 with default rescale. I'll try v0.8 (no rescale) and v1.0 (with bias-correct) and rerun.
ops-bot: deploy@r4-staging: new job 58231 queued by anya — tag: opal-int4-repro
nora: another angle: check KV cache dtype conversion and attention rotary scaling when quantizing. I've seen rotary overflow when scale factors are applied in different order and that only shows up on long contexts.
liam: agree. can you paste one failing example (input + expected vs actual) so we can inspect tokenization + logits?
anya: here's a redacted example that fails (intent: create appointment):
Input: "schedule follow-up with dr. chan next tuesday at 3pm"
Expected intent: CREATE_APPT
Model output (post-merge+int4): "I can look that up for you" (non-committal, wrong intent)
Tokenized lengths: pre-merge: 11 tokens; post-merge+int4: 11 tokens (no shift). Logit top-1 delta shows confidence drop from 0.93->0.42.
kevin: interesting — tokenization same but logits unstable. please run `--dump-logits` for that example with both merge orders and attach.
anya: did that, uploading snippets to the thread: diff shows attention scores at layer 18 are ~10-20% lower in int4 then float16 for the key positions.
liam: sounds like quant kernel precision at certain layers. plan: (1) rerun merge with v1.0 bias-correct, (2) try symmetric vs asymmetric quant params for those layers, (3) run per-layer mixed precision (keep critical layers in fp16) to find culprit.
nora: I'll set up a small sweep job — tag `opal-int4-sweep`. keep me posted.
anya: thanks — timeline: I'll run the v1.0 merge + symmetric quant sweep today and drop results by EOD. If we can't recover, propose fallback policy: serve customer on float16 Dedicated nodes until we diagnose.
kevin: +1 fallback. also file a quick postmortem with the eval pack examples so CS can see impact.
anya: will do. attaching summary CSV link: https://internal.redwood/ops/opal-int4-eval-summary.csv :thumbsup:
liam: cool. ping me when the v1.0 runs finish and I will run kernel-level traces.
nora: adding to the Ops board and scheduling a short sync with infra tomorrow 10am.
anya: thanks everyone :heart:
